definition: To call 'p' true is just to assert p: '"p" is true' is equivalent to p, and any sentence apt for sincere assertion, moral sentences included, can be called true. A quasi-realist expressivist can say in this sense that 'murder is wrong' is true while denying that it represents a moral fact.
note: No pinned witness yet (e.g. Horwich on minimalism, Blackburn on quasi-realism). Recorded so that the emotivism results are not read as covering an expressivist who accepts minimal truth; #182 and #185 are to source and formalize that rival.
